separable: separable — *tack on a service fee* or *tack a service fee on*; with a pronoun it must split: *tack it on*, never ✗ *tack on it*. The thing it is added to takes *to*: *tacked on to the bill*.
gloss: To add something extra at the end, often something small or unwelcome.
examples: The hotel *tacks on* a resort fee nobody mentions at booking.
They *tacked* two more questions *on* at the end of the form.
A delivery charge had been *tacked on* without any warning.

ru: увязываться, увязаться (за кем-л.); идти следом, пойти следом
separable: nothing to separate — the verb takes no object; the people you follow come after *with*: *tag along with us*.
gloss: To go somewhere with other people who did not really invite you.
examples: Do you mind if I *tag along*?
Her little brother *tagged along* to every practice.
He's been *tagging along* with the crew all summer.
contrast: *tag* doubles its *g* before an ending: *tagged along*, *tagging along*.

separable: separable — *tally up the votes* or *tally the votes up*; with a pronoun it must split: *tally them up*.
gloss: To add numbers or items together to get a total.
examples: Let's *tally up* what we each owe.
She *tallied* the receipts *up* at closing time.
Once the mail-in ballots were *tallied up*, the race had flipped.
contrast: the *-y* becomes *-ies* and *-ied*: *tallies up*, *tallied up* — but *-ing* keeps the *y*: *tallying up*.

separable: separable — *talk over the offer* or *talk the offer over*; with a pronoun it must split: *talk it over*, never ✗ *talk over it*.
gloss: To discuss something carefully with someone before deciding.
examples: Let me *talk it over* with my wife and call you tomorrow.
We *talked over* the budget for two hours.
They're still *talking over* whether to move.

separable: always split — the person goes in the middle: *talk her into it*, never ✗ *talk into her*. What follows *into* is a noun or an *-ing* form: *talked me into buying it*.
gloss: To persuade someone to do something they were not planning to do.
examples: Don't let him *talk* you *into* another timeshare.
She *talked* her parents *into* letting her go.
I got *talked into* running the half marathon.

separable: always split — the person goes in the middle: *talk him out of it*, never ✗ *talk out of him*. What follows *out of* is a noun or an *-ing* form.
gloss: To persuade someone not to do something they were planning to do.
examples: His friends *talked* him *out of* quitting.
You can't *talk* her *out of* anything once she's decided.
I was *talked out of* selling the car, and I'm glad.

separable: nothing to separate — the verb takes no object; the person comes after *to*: *talk back to your mother*.
gloss: To answer someone in authority rudely.
examples: Don't *talk back* to your teacher.
He *talked back* once and lost his phone for a week.
She's been *talking back* to everybody since she turned thirteen.

separable: inseparable — the person always follows the whole phrase: *talks down to his staff*, never ✗ *talks his staff down to*.
gloss: To speak to someone as if they were less intelligent than you.
examples: The doctor never *talks down to* patients.
She felt *talked down to* in every meeting.
Stop *talking down to* me — I read the report too.

separable: separable — *talk up the new album* or *talk the new album up*; with a pronoun it must split: *talk it up*.
gloss: To praise something publicly so that other people get interested in it.
examples: The coach keeps *talking up* his freshman quarterback.
They *talked* the neighborhood *up* until prices doubled.
The movie was *talked up* so much that it couldn't possibly deliver.

ru: разбирать по шагам, разобрать по шагам; подробно объяснять, объяснить
separable: separable — *talk through the steps* or *talk the steps through*; with a pronoun it must split: *talk it through*. It also takes a person plus a thing: *talk me through the setup*.
gloss: To go over something step by step with someone until it is clear.
examples: Can you *talk* me *through* the installation?
We *talked through* every objection before the vote.
She's *talking* the new hire *through* the checklist right now.

separable: separable — *tamp down expectations* or *tamp expectations down*; with a pronoun it must split: *tamp them down*.
gloss: To reduce or hold back something that is growing too strong, like fear or excitement.
examples: The mayor tried to *tamp down* the panic.
Management *tamped* the rumors *down* with a company-wide email.
Prices are finally being *tamped down* by higher rates.

separable: separable — *tangle up the cords* or *tangle the cords up*; with a pronoun it must split: *tangle them up*. Very often passive: *get tangled up in something*.
transitivity: both — transitive (*the wind tangled up the flag*), intransitive (*the leash tangles up every walk*)
gloss: To twist something into a knot, or to get caught up in a mess you cannot easily get out of.
examples: The headphones *tangle up* the second you put them in a pocket.
He *tangled* the fishing line *up* on the first cast.
She got *tangled up* in a lawsuit that lasted three years.

ru: получать доступ, получить доступ (к); использовать, задействовать
separable: inseparable — what you reach always follows the whole phrase: *tap into the market*, never ✗ *tap the market into*.
gloss: To start using a supply of money, energy, or interest that was already there.
examples: The ad *taps into* a real fear about money.
They *tapped into* savings to cover the roof.
He's *tapping into* a market nobody else noticed.
contrast: *tap* doubles its *p* before an ending: *tapped into*, *tapping into*.

separable: nothing to separate — the verb takes no object: *he tapped out in the third round*. Informal.
gloss: To quit or give up because you have nothing left.
examples: I'm *tapping out* — somebody else can finish the shift.
He *tapped out* after two hours of moving furniture.
Half the volunteers had *tapped out* by noon.
contrast: as an adjective, *tapped out* means out of money: *I'm tapped out until Friday*.

separable: separable — *tape up the box* or *tape the box up*; with a pronoun it must split: *tape it up*.
gloss: To close or bind something with tape.
examples: *Tape up* the boxes before the movers get here.
The trainer *taped* his ankle *up* at halftime.
Every window was *taped up* before the storm.
contrast: *tape* drops its *e* before *-ing*: *taping up*, not ✗ *tapeing up*.

ru: постепенно уменьшаться, уменьшиться; сходить на нет, сойти на нет
separable: usually no object at all: *the rain tapered off*. When it does take one, keep it together: *taper off the medication*, not ✗ *taper the medication off*.
transitivity: both — intransitive (*sales tapered off*), transitive (*taper off the dose*)
gloss: To become gradually smaller or weaker until it stops.
examples: Traffic *tapers off* after seven.
The applause *tapered off* and the room went quiet.
Her doctor is *tapering off* the steroids over three weeks.

separable: inseparable — the person always follows the whole phrase: *tattled on his sister*, never ✗ *tattled his sister on*. Mostly children's English.
gloss: To tell an adult that another child has done something wrong.
examples: Nobody likes a kid who *tattles on* everyone.
She *tattled on* her brother for eating the cookies.
He's been *tattling on* the whole class all week.

separable: nothing to separate — the verb takes no object; the partner comes after *with*: *team up with a local charity*.
gloss: To join with another person or group to work on something together.
examples: Let's *team up* for the group project.
The two schools *teamed up* to run the food drive.
They're *teaming up* with a startup in Austin.

separable: separable — *tee up the next question* or *tee the next question up*; with a pronoun it must split: *tee it up*.
gloss: To get something ready so that it can happen next.
examples: Her opening remarks *tee up* the whole debate.
We *teed up* three interviews for Thursday.
The vote has been *teed up* for early next month.
contrast: *tee* keeps both *e*s and adds *-d* or *-ing*: *teed up*, *teeing up*.

ru: выводить из себя, вывести из себя; злить, разозлить
separable: separable — the person goes in the middle with a pronoun: *that teed me off*; with a noun either order works: *teed off the whole staff*. Usually heard in the passive: *he was teed off*. Informal.
gloss: To make someone annoyed or angry.
examples: Little things like that *tee* him *off*.
The surprise fee *teed off* half the customers.
She was *teed off* about being left out of the email.
contrast: in golf *tee off* means to start a round: *we tee off at eight*.

separable: separable — *test out the new oven* or *test the new oven out*; with a pronoun it must split: *test it out*, never ✗ *test out it*.
gloss: To try something in order to see whether it works.
examples: Let's *test out* the projector before everyone shows up.
He *tested* the theory *out* on his own students.
The feature is being *tested out* with a few hundred users.

separable: separable when it takes an object — *thaw out the chicken* or *thaw the chicken out*; with a pronoun it must split: *thaw it out*. It is just as common with no object: *the pipes thawed out*.
transitivity: both — transitive (*thaw out the steaks*), intransitive (*the ground is thawing out*)
gloss: To stop being frozen, or to make something stop being frozen.
examples: *Thaw out* the shrimp in cold water, not on the counter.
The lake finally *thawed out* in April.
My hands are still *thawing out* from the walk.

separable: separable when it takes an object — *thin out the seedlings* or *thin the seedlings out*; with a pronoun it must split: *thin them out*. Usually there is no object: *the crowd thinned out*.
transitivity: both — intransitive (*traffic thins out after nine*), transitive (*thin out the carrots*)
gloss: To become fewer or less dense, or to make something fewer or less dense.
examples: The crowd *thins out* once the headliner finishes.
His hair *thinned out* in his thirties.
We spent Saturday *thinning out* the tomato plants.
contrast: *thin* doubles its *n* before an ending: *thinned out*, *thinning out*.

separable: inseparable — what you look through always follows the whole phrase: *thumb through a magazine*, never ✗ *thumb a magazine through*.
gloss: To turn the pages of something quickly without reading carefully.
examples: He *thumbs through* the catalog every time it comes.
She *thumbed through* the report on the way to the meeting.
I was *thumbing through* an old photo album and found this.
contrast: the *b* in *thumb* is silent: *thumbed* sounds like THUMD.

separable: separable — with a pronoun it must split: *that ticks me off*, never ✗ *ticks off me*; with a noun either order works: *ticked off the neighbors*. Very often passive: *I'm ticked off*. Informal.
gloss: To make someone angry or irritated.
examples: It really *ticks* me *off* when people don't signal.
His joke *ticked off* everyone at the table.
She's still *ticked off* about the parking ticket.

ru: выручать, выручить; помогать продержаться, помочь продержаться
separable: separable, and the person almost always goes in the middle: *tide me over*, *this will tide you over until Friday*, never ✗ *tide over me*.
gloss: To give someone enough of something to get through a difficult period.
examples: Take twenty dollars — it should *tide* you *over* until payday.
A snack *tided* the kids *over* until dinner.
The loan is just *tiding* them *over* through the slow season.

ru: прибирать, прибрать; наводить порядок, навести порядок
separable: separable when it takes an object — *tidy up the kitchen* or *tidy the kitchen up*; with a pronoun it must split: *tidy it up*. Often no object at all: *let's tidy up before they get here*.
transitivity: both — transitive (*tidy up the desk*), intransitive (*I tidied up after dinner*)
gloss: To make a place neat by putting things where they belong.
examples: Can you *tidy up* the living room?
She *tidied* the whole apartment *up* in an hour.
He's *tidying up* his notes before he hands them in.
contrast: the *-y* becomes *-ies* and *-ied*: *tidies up*, *tidied up* — but *-ing* keeps it: *tidying up*.

separable: separable — *tie up the newspapers* or *tie the newspapers up*; with a pronoun it must split: *tie it up*, never ✗ *tie up it*.
gloss: To fasten something with rope or string so it cannot move or come apart.
examples: *Tie up* the trash bag before the raccoons find it.
He *tied* the boat *up* at the dock.
The robbers had *tied up* the guard and taken the keys.
contrast: the *-ing* form is *tying up*, not ✗ *tieing up*.

separable: separable — *tie up the phone line*, *tie the line up*, *tie it up*. In this meaning it is mostly passive with people: *I'm tied up until three*.
gloss: To keep someone or something busy or unavailable for a while.
examples: Sorry, I'm *tied up* in meetings all morning.
The accident *tied up* traffic for two hours.
Inventory *ties up* most of their cash.

ru: связывать по рукам и ногам; ограничивать, ограничить; привязывать, привязать
separable: separable — *tie down the tarp* or *tie the tarp down*; with a pronoun it must split: *tie it down*. Of people, usually passive: *I don't want to be tied down*.
gloss: To fasten something so it cannot move, or to limit someone's freedom.
examples: *Tie down* everything in the truck bed.
A mortgage *tied* them *down* more than they expected.
He's never wanted to be *tied down* to one city.

separable: usually no object — what it connects to comes after *with*: *ties in with the main story*. When it does take an object it splits: *tie the ending in with the opening*.
transitivity: both — intransitive (*that ties in nicely*), transitive (*tie the lesson in with the reading*)
gloss: To connect or fit well with something else.
examples: How does this *tie in* with what we discussed?
The ad campaign *tied in* with the movie release.
She's *tying* the survey results *in* with last year's numbers.

separable: separable when it takes an object — *tighten up security* or *tighten security up*; with a pronoun it must split: *tighten it up*. Also used with no object: *the defense tightened up*.
transitivity: both — transitive (*tighten up the rules*), intransitive (*his shoulders tightened up*)
gloss: To make something stricter, tighter, or better organized.
examples: We need to *tighten up* the hiring process.
The airline *tightened* its refund policy *up* last year.
Security has been *tightened up* since the break-in.

separable: separable when it takes an object — *tip over the bucket* or *tip the bucket over*; with a pronoun it must split: *tip it over*. Just as often there is no object: *the lamp tipped over*.
transitivity: both — transitive (*the dog tipped over his water bowl*), intransitive (*the canoe tipped over*)
gloss: To fall onto its side, or to push something onto its side.
examples: That bookshelf will *tip over* if you don't anchor it.
She *tipped* the wheelbarrow *over* by accident.
Two chairs had been *tipped over* in the scuffle.
contrast: *tip* doubles its *p* before an ending: *tipped over*, *tipping over*.

ru: предупреждать, предупредить (тайно); давать наводку, дать наводку
separable: separable — *tip off the police* or *tip the police off*; with a pronoun it must split: *tip them off*, never ✗ *tip off them*.
gloss: To secretly warn someone about something, especially something illegal or about to happen.
examples: One careless question can *tip off* the seller.
A neighbor *tipped* the police *off* about the noise.
The suspects had clearly been *tipped off*.

separable: separable — *tire out the kids* or *tire the kids out*; with a pronoun it must split: *tire them out*, never ✗ *tire out them*.
gloss: To make someone completely exhausted.
examples: A long walk *tires out* the puppy for the whole evening.
The hike *tired* us *out* more than we expected.
She was *tired out* before the day even started.
contrast: *tired out* here is a real past form; *tired* alone is also the everyday adjective: *I'm tired*.

separable: separable — *tone down the language* or *tone the language down*; with a pronoun it must split: *tone it down*, never ✗ *tone down it*.
gloss: To make something less strong, less extreme, or less loud.
examples: *Tone it down* — the baby is asleep.
The studio *toned down* the ending after test screenings.
His speech had been *toned down* by the lawyers.

ru: подтягивать, подтянуть (мышцы); приводить в форму, привести в форму
separable: separable when it takes an object — *tone up your arms* or *tone your arms up*; with a pronoun it must split: *tone them up*. Also used with no object: *I'm trying to tone up*.
transitivity: both — transitive (*tone up your legs*), intransitive (*she's toning up for the wedding*)
gloss: To make muscles firmer and stronger through exercise.
examples: Swimming *tones up* your whole back.
He *toned* his core *up* over one winter.
She's been *toning up* since January.

separable: separable — *top off the tank* or *top the tank off*; with a pronoun it must split: *top it off*, never ✗ *top off it*.
gloss: To fill something the rest of the way to the top.
examples: Can I *top off* your coffee?
He *topped* the tank *off* before the road trip.
The pool gets *topped off* every couple of weeks in summer.
contrast: *top* doubles its *p* before an ending: *topped off*, *topping off*.

separable: separable — *top off the meal with dessert*, *top the evening off*; with a pronoun it must split, and the fixed phrase *to top it off* means "and on top of everything else".
gloss: To finish something in a memorable way, usually with one last thing.
examples: They *topped off* the weekend with a barbecue.
A pay raise *topped* the year *off* nicely.
And to *top it off*, my flight was canceled.

ru: достигать максимума, достичь максимума; выходить на предел, выйти на предел
separable: nothing to separate — the verb takes no object; the number comes after *at*: *topped out at 95 degrees*.
gloss: To reach the highest level and go no higher.
examples: The trail *tops out* at nine thousand feet.
Sales *topped out* in 2019 and slid after that.
Temperatures are *topping out* in the low nineties this week.

separable: separable — *toss out the leftovers* or *toss the leftovers out*; with a pronoun it must split: *toss it out*, never ✗ *toss out it*.
gloss: To throw something away because you no longer want it.
examples: Just *toss out* anything that's expired.
He *tossed* the whole box *out* without looking inside.
Two bags of clothes were *tossed out* in the cleanup.
contrast: *toss* adds *-es* in the third person: *tosses out*, not ✗ *tosss out*.

separable: separable — *toss out the case* or *toss the case out*; with a pronoun it must split: *toss it out*. Common in news about courts.
gloss: To reject or dismiss something officially.
examples: The judge could *toss out* the whole lawsuit.
An appeals court *tossed* the conviction *out*.
Their proposal was *tossed out* in the first round.

separable: separable — *toss around a few ideas* or *toss a few ideas around*; with a pronoun it must split: *toss them around*.
gloss: To discuss ideas or suggestions informally, without deciding yet.
examples: We're *tossing around* a few names for the store.
They *tossed* the idea *around* over lunch.
That number has been *tossed around* for months with no proof.

separable: separable — *touch up the paint* or *touch the paint up*; with a pronoun it must split: *touch it up*, never ✗ *touch up it*.
gloss: To improve something with small corrections or additions.
examples: I need to *touch up* the trim around the door.
She *touched* her makeup *up* before the photos.
Every picture in the catalog has been *touched up*.
contrast: *touch* adds *-es* in the third person: *touches up*.

separable: nothing to separate — the verb takes no object: *the plane touched down at six*.
gloss: To land, said of an aircraft or of a tornado reaching the ground.
examples: We *touch down* in Denver at 4:15.
The flight *touched down* twenty minutes early.
A tornado had *touched down* just west of town.

separable: separable, though the object is usually long and stays at the end: *touched off a wave of protests*; with a pronoun it splits: *touched it off*.
gloss: To cause something big and sudden to start, like a fight or a panic.
examples: One rumor can *touch off* a run on the bank.
The verdict *touched off* protests in three cities.
A single spark *touched off* the fire that burned the block.

ru: связываться, связаться; выходить на связь, выйти на связь
separable: fixed — the object is always *base* and nothing else goes there: *touch base with the client*, never ✗ *touch the base*. The person comes after *with*. Common in American work English.
transitivity: transitive — but only with the fixed object *base*
gloss: To make brief contact with someone to share news or check on something.
examples: Let's *touch base* on Monday.
I *touched base* with the vendor this morning.
She's *touching base* with everyone before the launch.

ru: терпеть, вытерпеть; выдерживать, выдержать; держаться до конца
separable: fixed — the object is always *it*: *tough it out*, never ✗ *tough the winter out*. Informal.
transitivity: transitive — but only with the fixed object *it*
gloss: To keep going through something painful or difficult instead of giving up.
examples: No painkillers — he just *toughs it out*.
They *toughed it out* through two years of construction.
She's *toughing it out* until the contract ends.

separable: separable when it takes an object — *toughen up the rules* or *toughen the rules up*; with a pronoun it must split: *toughen him up*. Often no object: *you'll toughen up*.
transitivity: both — intransitive (*he toughened up fast*), transitive (*boot camp toughened them up*)
gloss: To become stronger and better able to handle hardship, or to make someone or something stronger.
examples: You *toughen up* quickly on a job like that.
Two winters in Chicago *toughened* him *up*.
The state is *toughening up* its emissions rules.

ru: эвакуировать (машину); увозить на эвакуаторе, увезти на эвакуаторе
separable: separable — *tow away the car* or *tow the car away*; with a pronoun it must split: *tow it away*. Usually passive: *my car got towed away*.
gloss: To pull a vehicle away with a truck, usually because it is parked illegally or broken down.
examples: They *tow away* anything left overnight in that lot.
The city *towed* my van *away* on street-cleaning day.
Three cars were being *towed away* when I walked by.
contrast: *tow* rhymes with *go*, not with *now*: TOH, and the past is *towed*, not ✗ *toed*.

separable: separable — *track down the owner* or *track the owner down*; with a pronoun it must split: *track him down*, never ✗ *track down him*.
gloss: To find someone or something after searching hard.
examples: It took a week to *track down* the right part.
She *tracked* her birth mother *down* through a DNA site.
Police are still *tracking down* witnesses.

ru: сдавать в зачёт, сдать в зачёт (старое при покупке нового)
separable: separable — *trade in your old phone* or *trade your old phone in*; with a pronoun it must split: *trade it in*. What you get instead comes after *for*.
gloss: To give something old to a seller as part of the payment for something new.
examples: You can *trade in* the old console for store credit.
They *traded* the minivan *in* for a pickup.
My laptop was *traded in* for about two hundred dollars.

ru: менять на лучшее, поменять на лучшее; переходить на более дорогое
separable: nothing to separate — the verb takes no object; what you move to comes after *to*: *trade up to a bigger house*.
gloss: To replace what you have with a better or more expensive version.
examples: A lot of buyers *trade up* after the first kid.
They *traded up* to a three-bedroom last spring.
She's *trading up* to a better camera this year.

ru: затихать, затихнуть; смолкать, смолкнуть; сходить на нет
separable: nothing to separate — the verb takes no object: *her voice trailed off*.
gloss: To get quieter and quieter until it stops, especially a voice.
examples: He starts a story and then just *trails off*.
Her voice *trailed off* when she saw who was listening.
The applause was *trailing off* by the time she reached the stage.

separable: nothing to separate — the verb takes no object: *the guests trickled in*.
gloss: To arrive slowly, a few at a time, instead of all at once.
examples: People *trickle in* for about an hour after the doors open.
Results *trickled in* all night.
Donations are still *trickling in* from the mailing.

ru: сбивать с толку, сбить с толку; ошибаться, ошибиться; подставлять подножку
separable: separable when it takes an object — *the question tripped her up*, *tripped up a lot of students*; with a pronoun it must split: *trip you up*. Also used with no object: *he tripped up on the last line*.
transitivity: both — transitive (*that detail trips people up*), intransitive (*she tripped up once*)
gloss: To make a mistake, or to cause someone to make one.
examples: Irregular verbs *trip up* almost everybody.
The lawyer *tripped* the witness *up* on a date.
He's *tripping up* over the same two sounds every time.
contrast: *trip* doubles its *p* before an ending: *tripped up*, *tripping up*.

ru: вытаскивать на свет, вытащить на свет; приводить одни и те же доводы
separable: separable — *trot out the same excuse* or *trot the same excuse out*; with a pronoun it must split: *trot it out*. Usually disapproving.
gloss: To bring up the same old argument, story, or excuse again.
examples: Every election they *trot out* the same slogans.
He *trotted* that story *out* at dinner again.
The statistic keeps being *trotted out* without context.
contrast: *trot* doubles its *t* before an ending: *trotted out*, *trotting out*.

separable: separable in principle — *trump up charges*, *trump them up* — but it is almost always heard in the passive or before a noun: *trumped-up charges*.
gloss: To invent a false accusation against someone.
examples: They *trumped up* a theft charge to keep him in jail.
The journalist was arrested on *trumped-up* charges.
Investigators found the department had been *trumping up* violations for years.

separable: separable — *try on the jacket* or *try the jacket on*; with a pronoun it must split: *try it on*, never ✗ *try on it*.
gloss: To put on a piece of clothing to see whether it fits and looks right.
examples: *Try on* the other size before you decide.
She *tried* four dresses *on* and bought none of them.
He's *trying on* boots in the back.
contrast: the *-y* becomes *-ies* and *-ied*: *tries on*, *tried on* — but *-ing* keeps it: *trying on*.

separable: separable — *try out the new app* or *try the new app out*; with a pronoun it must split: *try it out*, never ✗ *try out it*.
gloss: To use something for the first time to see how good it is.
examples: Let's *try out* that taco place on Fifth.
I *tried* the trial version *out* for a week.
The recipe is being *tried out* on the family first.

ru: проходить отбор, пройти отбор; пробоваться (в команду)
separable: inseparable — nothing goes inside: *try out for the team*, never ✗ *try the team out for*. American schools use this for sports and plays alike.
gloss: To compete or audition for a place on a team or in a performance.
examples: She's going to *try out for* varsity in the fall.
He *tried out for* the school play and got the lead.
Forty kids are *trying out for* twelve spots.

ru: укладывать спать, уложить спать; укрывать, укрыть (одеялом)
separable: separable — *tuck in the kids* or *tuck the kids in*; with a pronoun it must split: *tuck them in*, never ✗ *tuck in them*.
gloss: To put a child to bed and pull the covers snugly around them.
examples: Dad *tucks* them *in* every night.
She *tucked in* the twins and read one story.
He likes being *tucked in* even though he's nine.

separable: separable — *tuck in your shirt* or *tuck your shirt in*; with a pronoun it must split: *tuck it in*.
gloss: To push the bottom of a shirt inside your pants or skirt.
examples: *Tuck in* your shirt before the interview.
He *tucked* his shirt *in* and straightened his tie.
Her blouse was *tucked in* on one side only.

ru: убирать, убрать (подальше); прятать, спрятать; откладывать, отложить
separable: separable — *tuck away some money* or *tuck the money away*; with a pronoun it must split: *tuck it away*. Of places it is usually passive: *a café tucked away on a side street*.
gloss: To put something in a safe, hidden, or out-of-the-way place.
examples: She *tucks away* a little from every paycheck.
He *tucked* the letter *away* in a drawer.
The cabin is *tucked away* at the end of a dirt road.

ru: настраиваться, настроиться (на волну); смотреть, посмотреть; слушать передачу
separable: nothing to separate — the verb takes no object; the channel or show comes after *to*: *tune in to channel 7*.
gloss: To turn on a radio or television program in order to watch or listen.
examples: *Tune in* tomorrow at eight for the finale.
Nine million people *tuned in* to the debate.
Fans have been *tuning in* every Sunday since September.

ru: отключаться, отключиться; переставать слушать, перестать слушать
separable: separable when it takes an object — *tune out the noise* or *tune the noise out*; with a pronoun it must split: *tune it out*. Just as common with no object: *he tuned out halfway through*.
transitivity: both — transitive (*tune out the noise*), intransitive (*I tuned out after ten minutes*)
gloss: To stop paying attention to someone or something.
examples: Students *tune out* about forty minutes in.
She *tuned* the argument *out* and kept reading.
He's been *tuning out* the news for his own sanity.

separable: separable — *tune up the engine* or *tune the engine up*; with a pronoun it must split: *tune it up*. Musicians also use it with no object: *the orchestra is tuning up*.
transitivity: both — transitive (*tune up the car*), intransitive (*the band tuned up backstage*)
gloss: To adjust an engine or an instrument so that it runs or sounds right.
examples: Get the truck *tuned up* before winter.
He *tuned* the piano *up* the morning of the recital.
The orchestra was still *tuning up* when we sat down.

separable: separable — *turn off the light* or *turn the light off*; with a pronoun it must split: *turn it off*, never ✗ *turn off it*.
gloss: To stop a machine, light, or supply from running.
examples: *Turn off* the oven when the timer goes.
She *turned* the water *off* at the main.
Notifications have been *turned off* since Friday.
contrast: the opposite is *turn on*, and it splits the same way: *turn it on*, *turn it off*.

ru: отталкивать, оттолкнуть; вызывать отвращение, вызвать отвращение
separable: separable — with a pronoun it must split: *it turns me off*, never ✗ *turns off me*; with a noun either order works: *turned off a lot of voters*.
gloss: To make someone lose interest or feel disgusted.
examples: The smell of the place *turns* most people *off* immediately.
His tone *turned off* everyone in the room.
A lot of customers were *turned off* by the new pricing.

separable: separable — *turn down the offer* or *turn the offer down*; with a pronoun it must split: *turn it down*, never ✗ *turn down it*.
gloss: To refuse an offer, a request, or a person.
examples: You don't *turn down* a job like that.
They *turned* her *down* for the loan twice.
His application was *turned down* without explanation.

ru: убавлять, убавить; делать тише, сделать тише
separable: separable — *turn down the music* or *turn the music down*; with a pronoun it must split: *turn it down*.
gloss: To reduce the volume, heat, or brightness of something.
examples: *Turn down* the TV — I'm on the phone.
He *turned* the heat *down* to sixty-eight.
The lights were *turned down* for the slideshow.

ru: прибавлять, прибавить; делать громче, сделать громче
separable: separable — *turn up the volume* or *turn the volume up*; with a pronoun it must split: *turn it up*, never ✗ *turn up it*.
gloss: To increase the volume, heat, or intensity of something.
examples: *Turn up* the radio — this is my song.
She *turned* the thermostat *up* two degrees.
The pressure is being *turned up* on the mayor.

separable: nothing to separate — the verb takes no object: *he turned up an hour late*.
gloss: To arrive or appear somewhere, often unexpectedly.
examples: Half the guests *turn up* after eight.
He *turned up* at my door with no warning.
She's been *turning up* late all month.

separable: nothing to separate — the lost thing is the subject: *my keys turned up*.
gloss: To be found by chance after being lost.
examples: Lost phones usually *turn up* in the lost and found.
The ring *turned up* in the couch cushions.
Nothing has *turned up* in the search so far.

separable: separable — *turn in your homework* or *turn your homework in*; with a pronoun it must split: *turn it in*, never ✗ *turn in it*.
gloss: To hand something to a teacher, a boss, or an office.
examples: *Turn in* the permission slip by Friday.
She *turned* her resignation *in* on Monday.
Only nine essays have been *turned in*.

separable: nothing to separate — the verb takes no object: *I'm going to turn in*. Slightly old-fashioned but still common.
gloss: To go to bed.
examples: I think I'll *turn in* early tonight.
They *turned in* right after the news.
He was *turning in* around nine all week.

ru: сдавать полиции, сдать полиции; выдавать, выдать
separable: separable — with a pronoun it must split: *turn him in*, never ✗ *turn in him*; with a noun either order works. Reflexive use is common: *she turned herself in*.
gloss: To hand someone over to the police, including yourself.
examples: Reward money makes people *turn in* their own neighbors.
The suspect *turned* himself *in* Tuesday morning.
She was *turned in* by an anonymous caller.

separable: separable when it takes an object — *turn the car around*, *turn it around*. Just as common with no object: *turn around and look*.
transitivity: both — intransitive (*he turned around*), transitive (*turn the truck around*)
gloss: To face the other way, or to make something face or go the other way.
examples: *Turn around* — you've got something on your back.
She *turned* the car *around* at the state line.
He kept *turning around* to see who was following.

separable: separable — *turn around the company* or *turn the company around*; with a pronoun it must split: *turn it around*.
gloss: To change something failing into something successful.
examples: A new coach could *turn around* this season.
She *turned* the failing store *around* in two years.
The business has been *turned around* completely.

separable: separable when it takes an object — *turn over the pancakes* or *turn the pancakes over*; with a pronoun it must split: *turn it over*. Also with no object: *turn over and go back to sleep*.
transitivity: both — transitive (*turn the mattress over*), intransitive (*he turned over in bed*)
gloss: To move something so the other side is up, or to roll onto your other side.
examples: *Turn over* the card and read the answer.
He *turned* the burgers *over* too early.
She *turned over* and pulled the blanket up.

separable: separable — *turn over the documents* or *turn the documents over*; with a pronoun it must split: *turn them over*. The receiver comes after *to*: *turned it over to the FBI*.
gloss: To give something or someone to an authority that has the right to it.
examples: The company must *turn over* the emails by Friday.
They *turned* the suspect *over* to federal agents.
All the evidence has been *turned over* to the court.

separable: nothing to separate — it is followed by *to be*, by an adjective, or by a *that* clause: *it turned out that he was right*.
gloss: To prove in the end to be a certain way.
examples: It *turns out* she'd been right the whole time.
The rumor *turned out* to be false.
Everything is *turning out* better than we expected.

separable: nothing to separate — the verb takes no object: *thousands turned out*. The related noun is *turnout*.
gloss: To come to an event in a crowd.
examples: Hundreds *turn out* for the parade every year.
Only forty people *turned out* in the rain.
Voters have been *turning out* early all week.

separable: separable — *turn out the lights* or *turn the lights out*; with a pronoun it must split: *turn them out*. Used mainly of lights; for machines say *turn off*.
gloss: To switch off a light.
examples: *Turn out* the lights when you leave.
He *turned* the lamp *out* and lay there thinking.
Every light in the house had been *turned out*.

separable: inseparable when there is no other object — *turned into a nightmare*. In the transitive pattern the thing changed comes first: *turned the garage into an office*.
transitivity: both — intransitive (*it turned into a fight*), transitive (*they turned the attic into a bedroom*)
gloss: To become something different, or to change something into something different.
examples: A small disagreement can *turn into* a real fight.
They *turned* the old mill *into* apartments.
The drizzle was *turning into* sleet by dinnertime.

ru: не пускать, не пустить; отказывать, отказать (во входе)
separable: separable — *turn away customers* or *turn customers away*; with a pronoun it must split: *turn them away*. Often passive: *we were turned away at the door*.
gloss: To refuse to let someone in or to help them.
examples: The shelter never *turns away* anyone in winter.
They *turned* us *away* because we had no reservation.
Dozens of families were *turned away* at the border.

ru: поворачивать назад, повернуть назад; возвращаться, вернуться
separable: usually no object — *we turned back at the pass*. With an object it splits: *turn the hikers back*.
transitivity: both — intransitive (*they turned back*), transitive (*the storm turned the climbers back*)
gloss: To go back the way you came, or to make someone go back.
examples: If the road is flooded, *turn back*.
We *turned back* two miles from the summit.
Rangers were *turning* hikers *back* all afternoon.

ru: ополчаться, ополчиться (на); восстанавливать против, восстановить против
separable: inseparable when there is no other object — *the crowd turned against him*. In the transitive pattern the person influenced comes first: *turned the kids against their father*.
transitivity: both — intransitive (*voters turned against the plan*), transitive (*he turned them against her*)
gloss: To stop supporting someone and start opposing them, or to make someone do that.
examples: Public opinion *turns against* a mayor fast in a scandal.
His own party *turned against* him after the vote.
She accused him of *turning* the children *against* her.

separable: separable — *type up the notes* or *type the notes up*; with a pronoun it must split: *type them up*, never ✗ *type up them*.
gloss: To turn handwritten or spoken material into a typed document.
examples: Can you *type up* the minutes from Tuesday?
She *typed* her notes *up* the same evening.
The interview is being *typed up* right now.
contrast: *type* drops its *e* before *-ing*: *typing up*, not ✗ *typeing up*.

separable: separable — *type in the code* or *type the code in*; with a pronoun it must split: *type it in*.
gloss: To enter information using a keyboard.
examples: *Type in* the code they texted you.
He *typed* the address *in* wrong twice.
Your password is never stored after it's *typed in*.
